name: Brazil

findings.summary: TIM named Ericsson and Huawei as its initial 5G radio-access suppliers in December 2021, on non-exclusive terms, and renewed 4G and 5G supply contracts with both vendors in May 2023. Values undisclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Huawei's share of TIM's RAN versus Ericsson's is not disclosed; core vendor not confirmed. Vivo and Claro vendor splits not established in this pass. Ericsson is a third-pole (EU) supplier on the same network.

findings.reversal_of: Huawei eligibility to supply the federal government's private 5G network
findings.summary: The communications minister said Huawei was not eligible to supply the government's dedicated private 5G network under Anatel's auction-notice supplier governance requirements and a ministerial ordinance, while remaining free to supply commercial operators.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded as a partial exclusion (government network only), not a national ban. Tier 3 assigned as the tier of the procurement Huawei was excluded from; no award existed to reverse. The source says Huawei's private-company status conflicts with the governance criteria; that is the outlet's characterisation, not a quoted rule.

findings.summary: A data-centre campus for ByteDance in Pecém's export processing zone began preliminary works in January 2026; phase one is 200 MW IT, targeting operation from Q3 2027 and serving users outside Brazil.
findings.analyst_inference: Controller pole is contested between sources: Poder360 names Omnia (Pátria-controlled) as developer, DCD (Oct 2025) describes the project as ByteDance-led with Casa dos Ventos. Coded domestic on the later Omnia account; Pátria's corporate domicile not verified here. Tenant ByteDance is PRC. DCD cited about R$50bn; not converted.

findings.summary: Omnia signed a 20-year, US$2 billion self-production power deal with Casa dos Ventos, taking an undisclosed stake in wind parks (mainly the 630 MW Ibiapaba complex) to supply the Pecém TikTok data centre.
findings.analyst_inference: Single source fetched; The Next Web also reported the deal (seen in search, not fetched). Value as announced in USD by the source.

findings.local_actor: Municipality of Eldorado do Sul; Rio Grande do Sul state government
findings.summary: Eldorado do Sul enacted a municipal law enabling Scala's 'AI City' campus: 54 MW initial IT capacity, up to 4.75 GW potential. As of March 2026 the project remained in masterplan and permitting.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: neither source names Scala's parent; Scala is widely reported as DigitalBridge-backed (US), but that was not verified in this pass. Announced value is the full-campus estimate; phase one was put at US$500 million. Coded tier 2 because licences were still pending and construction start is unconfirmed; no tenant named.

findings.summary: The LNCC's Santos Dumont supercomputer completed a roughly fourfold upgrade by Eviden using Nvidia H100 and Grace Hopper plus AMD MI300A accelerators, described as the first major investment under the Brazilian AI Plan (PBIA).
findings.analyst_inference: Pole coded us for the accelerators (Nvidia and AMD dominate the GPU count); the facility itself is domestic (LNCC) and the integrator is EU. Upgrade cost not disclosed.

findings.summary: Serpro signed a contract with MeetKai Brasil to supply model families, code and weights for a sovereign government AI that Serpro will own and train on national data in its own data centres. Value undisclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded domestic because Serpro is to own the weights and hosting; the supplier MeetKai is US-origin, so base-model provenance and update dependence are open questions. A separate from-scratch PBIA LLM depends on a federal supercomputer purchase.

findings.local_actor: Rio de Janeiro state government (Governor Cláudio Castro)
findings.summary: During an official mission to China, Rio de Janeiro's governor signed agreements with Hikvision and Dahua to expand state video surveillance across all 92 municipalities; type, value and camera numbers of the agreements were not reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded tier 1 because neither source says whether the agreements are binding contracts. Revista Oeste cites about 5,800 cameras including facial recognition, which may conflate the existing vehicle-camera fleet.

findings.summary: Rio de Janeiro state had bought 21,571 Hikvision body cameras, about 13,000 in operation with the Military Police, according to an April 2025 report.
findings.analyst_inference: Purchase date not stated; operational as of April 2025. Whether footage or analytics depend on Hikvision cloud/update channels is not known.

research_gaps: RAN and core vendor shares for Vivo and Claro (Huawei vs Ericsson/Nokia) and TIM's core vendor.
Final text of the Anatel 5G notice/ordinance on government-network supplier criteria, and whether the private federal network was ever awarded (and to whom).
Who controls the Pecém TikTok campus: Omnia/Pátria versus ByteDance-led accounts; Pátria's domicile; whether ByteDance owns any equity.
Scala Data Centers' ultimate parent (reported DigitalBridge) and whether AI City construction has actually begun; any named hyperscaler tenant.
Base model and value of the Serpro-MeetKai contract; status of the PBIA federal supercomputer purchase and from-scratch Brazilian LLM.
Whether the Rio Hikvision/Dahua agreements became binding procurements; other state safe-city programmes (Ceará, São Paulo Smart Sampa vendor).
Redata data-centre tax regime: enacted terms and beneficiaries not researched in this pass.
No dedicated reversal search beyond the 2021 government-network exclusion; a broader check is warranted.
